findings.reason: the search that bounds the change must be re-run against `skills/reckon-build/` and the current prompt contract, or the node edits sites that no longer match.
findings.text: the §2 table names `skills/reckon-ship/SKILL.md:941`, `references/worker-protocol.md:213`, `references/sprint-orchestration.md:412` and `:483` as the four prohibition sites; `skills/reckon-ship/` does not exist, `SKILL.md:941` is empty, `worker-protocol.md:213` now reads "Write your landing record to your own fragment path and never to the plan", and `sprint-orchestration.md:412/483` carry unrelated text, so the plan's claim that "these four are the whole of it" is unverified against the current tree

findings.reason: the plan should either add the parity assertions to the existing module or state why two modules must read the same skill files, because the parallel reader is the same class of duplicate the plan exists to remove.
findings.text: the plan's §5 deliverable adds a new skill-contract test file rather than extending `tests/test_skill_contracts.py`, which already reads `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md` and `references/sprint-orchestration.md` for content contracts and already owns the read-set token budget this plan also edits

findings.reason: a design text naming the composed archive as the write target re-introduces the shared-write-path the fragment default was introduced to remove, so the plan must name the fragment owner and point the worker at its own fragment.
findings.text: the plan's landed §2 text says the worker "appends its landing record to its own section of the plan and its evidence anchor to the cumulative evidence record", but the mechanism that owns that placement lives elsewhere and the record is now a composed output: `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` `_landing_fragment_paths` grants `docs/evidence/fragments/<plan>/<node-id>.html` as the node's fragment and `reckon/evidence.py:565` composes the cumulative record from those fragments

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module; its one artifact, `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py`, is a small interface (named locators) over the string-slicing it performs, so nothing substantial is hidden behind an interface wider than itself.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's own design text sends a worker's evidence anchor to "the cumulative evidence record" directly, but landing-record placement is owned by the per-node fragment mechanism in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` (`_landing_fragment_paths`) and composed by `reckon/evidence.py:565`, so the plan describes writing into the composed output rather than the fragment the owner grants.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan enumerates its contradiction surface against `skills/reckon-ship/` and a "cumulative evidence record", but that directory no longer exists (renamed to `skills/reckon-build/`, commit 790d5c571) and the landing record is now per-node fragments, so the plan's search was aimed at a tree the codebase has moved off.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan adds `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py` as a parallel layer over the skill-contract assertions already owned by `tests/test_skill_contracts.py`, and does not say why that existing module (which reads the same `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md`) cannot be extended instead.
